s1.syndrome_frame: Acute monocular vision loss with associated orbital and adnexal inflammation
salient_findings: Pain, numbness, and erythematous induration of the eyelids and forearm
Tense eyelid edema, chemosis, and corneal haze
Serous retinal detachment and macular whitening
key_facts: Patient is an obese man in his mid-30s
No prior systemic or ocular disorders
Heavy alcohol consumption the night prior
Took 2 buprenorphine hydrochloride/naloxone hydrochloride pills
Denies any trauma
Visual acuity is no light perception in the right eye and 20/20 in the left eye
Intraocular pressure is 37 mm Hg in the right eye and 21 mm Hg in the left eye
Creatinine level is 2.2 mg/dL
Creatine kinase level is 29,320 U/L
Periorbital soft-tissue swelling on noncontrast computed tomography
Severe disorganization of the retinal architecture on Optical Coherence Tomography
Delayed choroidal filling and poor vascular perfusion on Fluorescein Angiography

shortlist.label: Central Retinal Artery Occlusion
shortlist.why_kept: sudden vision loss in one eye with no light perception and retinal findings

shortlist.label: Posterior Scleritis
shortlist.why_kept: orbital and adnexal inflammation with severe disorganization of the retinal architecture

shortlist.label: Giant Cell Arteritis
shortlist.why_kept: acute monocular vision loss with associated orbital inflammation

shortlist.label: Orbital Cellulitis
shortlist.why_kept: periorbital soft-tissue swelling and signs of infection

shortlist.label: Purtscher Retinopathy
shortlist.why_kept: trauma-like retinopathy with vision loss and retinal findings after heavy alcohol consumption and possible drug-related effects

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with sudden vision loss, severe retinal damage, and systemic symptoms such as pain and erythema after heavy alcohol consumption and possible buprenorphine/naloxone toxicity is consistent with Purtscher Retinopathy, a condition often associated with head trauma, long bone fractures, or other forms of systemic distress.

rejected.label: Central Retinal Artery Occlusion
rejected.why: While it could explain the vision loss, the presence of systemic symptoms and the specific pattern of retinal damage on imaging studies are more suggestive of Purtscher Retinopathy.

rejected.label: Posterior Scleritis
rejected.why: This condition would more likely present with pain and decreased vision, but the imaging findings and the acute onset of severe retinal changes are not typical for posterior scleritis.

rejected.label: Giant Cell Arteritis
rejected.why: This condition is more common in older adults and typically presents with symptoms of temporal arteritis, which are not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Orbital Cellulitis
rejected.why: While the patient has periorbital swelling, the primary issue is the severe retinal damage and vision loss, which is not characteristic of orbital cellulitis alone.
